# Scaling

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/operations/resources/scaling.mdx

title: Scaling
ogImageTitle: Scaling
ogImageSubtitle: Scale your service to handle more traffic

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Scaling

Zeabur allows you to adjust the resources allocated to your services so they can handle varying workloads. You can scale vertically by increasing CPU and memory, and choose the right infrastructure tier for your needs.

## Vertical Scaling

Vertical scaling means increasing (or decreasing) the CPU and memory allocated to a single service instance.

To adjust resources:

1. Open your service in the Zeabur dashboard.
2. Go to **Settings**.
3. Under the **Resources** section, configure the desired CPU and memory limits.
4. Save your changes. The new resource allocation takes effect on the next deployment.

### Resource Plans

Zeabur offers several resource tiers. The default allocation is suitable for most lightweight services, but you can increase resources for more demanding workloads such as databases, build servers, or AI inference.

<Callout>
  Resource allocation directly affects billing. Higher CPU and memory limits result in higher costs. See [Pricing](/pricing) for details on per-unit pricing.
</Callout>

## Servers

For workloads that require guaranteed resources, predictable performance, or compliance with data residency requirements, Zeabur offers **Servers**. A server gives you an isolated compute environment that is not shared with other users.

Benefits of servers include:

- **Guaranteed resources** — No noisy-neighbor issues.
- **Custom regions** — Deploy in specific geographic locations.
- **Higher resource ceilings** — Run services that exceed shared cluster limits.

See [Servers](/server) for setup instructions and available configurations.

## Scaling Strategies

| Scenario | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| Occasional traffic spikes | Increase CPU/memory to handle peak load |
| Consistent high traffic | Use a server for predictable performance |
| Cost optimization | Right-size resources based on [metrics](/operations/monitoring/metrics) |
| Temporary inactivity | [Suspend](/operations/deployment/suspend-service) the service to stop billing |

## Monitoring Resource Usage

Use the [Metrics](/operations/monitoring/metrics) dashboard to monitor CPU, memory, and network usage in real time. This data helps you determine when to scale up or down. For cost analysis, check the [Service Usage](/operations/resources/service-usage) page.

# Invite Member

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/operations/team/invite-member.mdx

title: Invite Member
ogImageTitle: Invite Member
ogImageSubtitle: Invite team members to join the project

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components';

# Invite Member

<Callout type="info">
  This page describes **project collaborators** — people invited to a single project to help manage its services. If you want to share many projects, servers, and a single subscription across multiple people, you probably want a [**Team**](/team) instead. A Team is its own workspace with shared billing, members, and ownership of resources.
</Callout>

There may be two or more members in a project, 
project owner can invite member into the project to manage the services.

## How to invite member

### Step1: Open the project settings

First, open your project which you want to invite member. Click on the config button in the left top corner of the project page, you will be navigated to the project settings page.

![Project Config](/manage/invite/project-config.png)

### Step2: Invite member

Choose the team panel from the sidebar, you will see the invite member button in the team panel.

![Project Settings](/manage/invite/project-settings.png)

Fill in the email address of the member you want to invite, and click the invite button. The member will receive an email invitation to join the project.

You can also copy the invitation link and share it with the member you want to invite, then the member can just open the link to join the project.

![Invite Member](/manage/invite/invite.png)

## FAQ

- **Q: Can I invite a member who is not registered on zeabur?**
    - A: Currently, you can only invite members who have registered on zeabur.

- **Q: What permissions does the member have after joining the project?**
    - A: The member will have the same permissions as the project owner except for the ability to delete the project.

- **Q: Can I remove a member from the project?**
    - A: Yes, you can remove a member from the project in the team panel of the project settings page.

# Security Report

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/operations/team/security-report.mdx

title: Security Report
ogImageTitle: Security Report
ogImageSubtitle: AI-powered security analysis

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Security Report

Zeabur provides a built-in security report feature that uses AI analysis to detect potential security vulnerabilities in your applications.

The security report feature employs AI-powered intelligent analysis to check for many common security vulnerabilities (such as industry standards like OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25), including Secret Key exposure, SQL injection, XSS attacks, and more. With just one click, you can complete a scan and generate a report within 5-10 minutes.

## How to Generate a Security Report

### Step 1: Navigate to Service Page

Click on the service you want to check and select the **Security** tab.

![Security Report Page](https://cdn.zeabur.com/security-report/security-report-list.png)

### Step 2: Generate Report

Click the **"Generate Report"** button, and the system will begin analyzing your code.

<Callout type="info">
Whether your code is deployed from GitHub or uploaded locally, you can use the security report feature.
</Callout>

### Step 3: View Report

After waiting a few minutes, you can see the newly generated report in the list. Click on the report to view detailed content, including detected issues, risk levels, and their locations in the code.

![Security Report Details Page](https://cdn.zeabur.com/security-report/security-report-detail.png)

## How to Fix Security Issues

You can **copy** or **download** the report content and paste it into your preferred AI development tools (like Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) to let AI help you fix the code.

After making corrections, redeploy your code to resolve the security vulnerabilities.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What vulnerabilities does the security report check?

The security report feature checks for multiple common security vulnerabilities, including but not limited to:

- OWASP Top 10 (such as SQL injection, XSS attacks, etc.)
- CWE Top 25
- Secret Key and sensitive information exposure
- Insecure dependencies

### How long does scanning take?

Depending on code complexity and size, scanning typically takes 5-10 minutes.

### Can I download the report?

Yes. You can copy or download the report content for easy sharing with your team or pasting into AI development tools for fixing.

### Are reports saved?

Yes. All generated reports are saved in the list, and you can access historical records at any time.

# Partner Program

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/partner.mdx

title: Partner Program
ogImageTitle: Partner Program
ogImageSubtitle: Zeabur Partner Program

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Partner Program

The Zeabur Partner Program offers collaboration opportunities for instructors, event organizers, enterprise consultants, and system integrators to earn rewards by promoting or onboarding Zeabur.

## Two Partnership Models

### Education Partner

For **instructors, community leaders, hackathon organizers, and educational institutions**. Promote Zeabur through teaching and technical events using Event Codes that give attendees free trial access, and earn rewards based on retained paying users.

- Receive a dedicated Event Code for attendees
- Retention count and reward payout one month after the event
- Ideal for workshops, online courses, hackathons, and community events

[Learn more →](/partner/event-partner)

### Sales Partner

For **enterprise consultants, system integrators, and technology consulting firms**. Help enterprise clients or institutions adopt Zeabur and earn recurring commissions based on the stages you participate in.

- Ideal for large contracts, institutional procurement, and technical consulting
- Two-layer commission: per-deal tiered rate × contribution stage weighting
- Specific rates, thresholds, and terms are individually negotiated in each contract — not publicly disclosed

[Learn more →](/partner/sales-partner)

## How It Differs from the Referral Program

Zeabur also offers a [Referral Program](/rewards/referral) that lets any user earn rewards through referral codes. Key differences:

| Aspect | Referral Program | Partner Program |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who | Any user | Instructors / Organizers / Consultants / Integrators |
| How | Automatic referral code flow | Manual review and contract |
| Rewards | Referral code commissions (by tier) | Event retention rewards / Sales Partner commissions |
| Terms | Unified platform terms | Individually negotiated per contract |

<Callout type="info">
A single transaction can only go through the Referral Program or the Partner Program — **they do not stack**.
</Callout>

## How to Apply

Sign up at [partner.zeabur.com](https://partner.zeabur.com) and submit an application based on your partnership type:

- **Education Partner** — Provide event name, expected attendance, dates, and format.
- **Sales Partner** — Provide company information, expected client types, and engagement scale.

The Zeabur team will reach out after receiving your application to discuss terms.

# Education Partner

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/partner/event-partner.mdx

title: Education Partner
ogImageTitle: Education Partner
ogImageSubtitle: Partnership for instructors, hackathon organizers, and community events

import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components'

# Education Partner

The Education Partner program is for **instructors, community leaders, hackathon organizers, and educational institutions**. When you host a technical event, teach a course, or lead a workshop, you can use an Event Code to give attendees free Zeabur credits, and earn rewards based on how many attendees retain as paying users after the event.

## How It Works

<Steps>

### Apply

Sign up at [partner.zeabur.com](https://partner.zeabur.com) and describe your course or event plan.

### Receive an Event Code

Zeabur creates a dedicated Event Code for your event, which you can distribute to attendees.

### Run your event

Guide attendees through deploying projects on Zeabur during your course, workshop, or hackathon.

### Retention count

One month after the Event Code distribution period ends, Zeabur counts users who registered with your Event Code and are still paying.

### Claim rewards

Earn rewards based on the number of retained paying users.

</Steps>

## Event Code Mechanism

An Event Code is a unique code that, once redeemed, adds credits to the attendee's account balance. The credits can be spent on any paid service on Zeabur (deployments, servers, AI Hub, etc.):

- Each Event Code is tied to a specific event and has a clear validity window (typically ending at the close of the event day).
- Attendees can redeem by visiting the event sign-up link (`https://zeabur.com/events?code=...`), which redeems automatically upon registration, or by entering the code on the Billing page after logging in.
- See the [Redeem Event Code](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code) guide for the full redemption steps you can share with attendees.

<Callout type="info">
Event Code redemptions do not trigger the Referral Program's commission mechanism — Event Code credits are sponsored, not real payments. Referral commissions only apply when a user's actual payment succeeds.
</Callout>

## Face Value

Event Codes come in two face values: **US$24** or **US$29**. The structure is the Pro Plan first month (US$19) plus a usage buffer:

- **US$24** ($19 + $5 buffer): Suitable for deployment-focused workshops.
- **US$29** ($19 + $10 buffer): Suitable for hackathons, courses, or events with heavier AI Hub usage.

Both face values let attendees **upgrade to Pro Plan without adding a credit card for the first month** and experience the full Pro feature set; the difference is how much balance is left for services beyond the Pro monthly fee.

## Reward Calculation

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Counting period | One month after the Event Code distribution period ends |
| Retention criteria | Attendee registered via Event Code, upgraded to a paid plan, and is still active during the counting period |
| Base reward | US$5 per retained paying user |
| Payout method | Zeabur Credits or other agreed methods |

### Example

You host a workshop for 50 attendees and distribute an Event Code. One month later, 8 attendees are still using Zeabur and have upgraded to a paid plan. Your reward is 8 × US$5 = **US$40**.

### Larger Events, Higher Rewards

For larger hackathons, extended course series, or high-impact events, Zeabur may adjust the reward to **US$10 per retained paying user** based on event scale, organizer reach, and expected conversion. These arrangements are discussed with the Zeabur team in advance and noted on your application.

## Ideal Scenarios

- **Programming courses** — Students deploy course projects to the cloud.
- **Technical workshops** — Hands-on events where attendees experience the deployment flow in real time.
- **Hackathons** — Teams use Zeabur to rapidly deploy their projects.
- **Online courses** — Provide Event Codes for remote students to practice.
- **Community events** — Tech meetups and talks paired with demo environments.

## How to Apply

Sign up at [partner.zeabur.com](https://partner.zeabur.com) and submit an event partnership application with the event name, expected attendance, dates, and format. The Zeabur team will review and set up a dedicated Event Code for you.

For other questions, feel free to contact us through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

# Redeem Event Code

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code.mdx

title: Redeem Event Code
ogImageTitle: Redeem Event Code
ogImageSubtitle: How attendees redeem a Zeabur Event Code

import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components'

# Redeem Event Code

Event Codes are distributed by Zeabur Education Partners at talks, courses, workshops, or hackathons. They can be redeemed for trial credits on Zeabur, which can be used to upgrade a subscription plan, deploy projects, and access other paid features.

This page covers the two ways to redeem an Event Code. Event organizers can share this link directly with attendees to avoid answering the same questions repeatedly.

<Callout type="info">
Event Codes have an expiration date — redeeming too early or too late will fail. Note the validity period given by your event organizer.
</Callout>

## Method 1: Event Sign-up Link (Easiest, for users without a Zeabur account)

If you don't have a Zeabur account yet, use the event sign-up link. Append your Event Code to this URL:

```
https://zeabur.com/events?code=YOUR_EVENT_CODE
```

For example, if your Event Code is `i_love_zeabur`, open:

```
https://zeabur.com/events?code=i_love_zeabur
```

Follow the on-page flow to complete Zeabur registration. The event credits are redeemed into your new account automatically.

## Method 2: Manual Redemption via Billing Page (For users with an existing account)

<Steps>

### Log in to Zeabur

Log in at [zeabur.com/login](https://zeabur.com/login).

### Open account settings

Click your name in the top-left to open the menu, then click **Settings**.

![Open account settings](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code/step-2-open-settings.png)

### Switch to Billing and click "Redeem Credits"

Click **Billing** in the left sidebar, then click the **Redeem Credits** button in the "Account Credit" section.

![Switch to Billing and click Redeem Credits](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code/step-3-billing-redeem-credits.png)

### Enter the Event Code

Enter your Event Code in the dialog, then click **Redeem**. On success, you'll see a notification in the bottom-right corner and your account balance will update immediately.

![Enter the Event Code](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code/step-4-enter-code.png)

</Steps>

## After Redemption

The event credits go straight into your **account balance** and can be used for any paid service on Zeabur — deploying projects, renting servers, AI Hub, and so on. They behave exactly like credits you'd top up yourself.

![Event credits can be spent on deployments, servers, AI Hub, and more](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code/after-redeem-uses.png)

<Callout type="info">
**Want to upgrade to Pro Plan as well?** Head to the [Pricing page](https://zeabur.com/pricing#upgrade) and click upgrade (see [Pro Plan](/pricing/pro-plan)).

- **Your event credits cover the Pro monthly fee**: The credits are applied directly to the upgrade — no card required.
- **Your credits don't cover the fee**: Start Zeabur Pro's **14-day free trial** — once it ends, your event credits are applied first to the monthly fee.
</Callout>

## FAQ

### What can I use the event credits for?

Any paid item on Zeabur — deployments, databases, servers, AI Hub, etc. They're just regular account balance, identical to credits you'd top up yourself.

### Do I need to bind a credit card?

Redeeming the Event Code does **not** require a card. When upgrading to Pro, no card is needed as long as your event credits cover the first month; otherwise a card is required to cover the difference. A card is also required from the second month onward if you want to keep using Pro.

### Can I keep using Zeabur after the event?

Yes. To stay on Pro, bind a credit card and billing continues automatically. If you'd rather not keep paying, stay on the [Free plan](/pricing) — you can return to the [Pricing page](https://zeabur.com/pricing) to upgrade again anytime.

### What happens when my event credits run out?

- **On a paid plan**: The next invoice is charged to your bound credit card.
- **On the Free plan**: You won't be able to use paid resources beyond the free quota. You can [top up](https://zeabur.com/account/billing) or upgrade to keep going.

### Expired / invalid Event Code / other issues

- **Expired** — Expired codes cannot be recovered. Confirm the validity period with your event organizer.
- **Invalid** — Double-check for typos and correct capitalization.
- **Other** — Contact customer support through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

## Related

- [Education Partner](/partner/event-partner) — If you want to apply to become a Zeabur Education Partner and get your own Event Code
- [Redeem Prepaid Card](/partner/sales-partner/redeem-card) — Redeem a Zeabur prepaid card (Voucher) sold by third-party partners

# Sales Partner

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/partner/sales-partner.mdx

title: Sales Partner
ogImageTitle: Sales Partner
ogImageSubtitle: Sales Partner program details

import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components'

# Sales Partner

The Sales Partner program is for **enterprise consultants, system integrators, and technology consulting firms**. When you help enterprise clients, institutions, or organizations adopt Zeabur, you earn recurring commissions based on the stages you actually participate in.

## When It Applies

The Sales Partner program applies in the following scenarios:

- **Enterprise cloud migration** — Help businesses migrate existing services to Zeabur.
- **Institutional procurement** — Bulk or contract-based purchases by educational institutions, government agencies, or enterprise IT departments, including Vouchers, invoicing, and contract-required cases.
- **Technical consulting** — As a technical consultant or system integrator, incorporate Zeabur into the deployment plans you design for clients.
- **Long-term service partnerships** — Provide deployment, operations, or payment collection services to clients using Zeabur as the underlying platform.

If the amount is below the threshold and the user pays individually through self-service, use the [Referral Program](/rewards/referral) automatic flow instead. Specific thresholds and conditions are agreed individually in each contract.

<Callout type="info">
A single transaction can only go through the Referral Program or the Sales Partner path — **they do not stack**.
</Callout>

## Commission Structure

Sales Partner commissions combine two layers, calculated based on your actual involvement.

### Layer 1: Per-Deal Tiered Rate

Each deal is calculated independently using a progressive rate based on deal size. Rates are **individually negotiated** based on partner type, market positioning, and engagement scale — public standard rates are not disclosed.

### Layer 2: Contribution Stage Weighting

Your share of each deal is weighted by the stages you actually own. The four stages sum to 100%. Stages that Zeabur handles internally are not paid out.

| Stage | Definition | Attribution Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lead (Introduction) | Find the customer | Timestamp of when you facilitated the first contact between both parties (including creating a dedicated communication group) |
| Close (Contract) | Close the deal | Signed quote from both parties |
| Deliver (Service) | Service delivery | You handle all client-side questions and operational support without requiring the Zeabur engineering team |
| Collect (Payments) | Collect payments | You complete collection and invoicing without Zeabur needing to chase |

### Common Participation Patterns

| Scenario | Lead | Close | Deliver | Collect |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Full service | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Introduction only | ✓ |   |   |   |
| Introduction + Service | ✓ |   | ✓ |   |
| Service + Collect |   |   | ✓ | ✓ |
| Close + operations (no Lead) |   | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Introduction + Service + Collect | ✓ |   | ✓ | ✓ |

### Multi-Party Splits

Different stages of the same deal can be owned by different partners. Each deal is calculated in isolation (no cross-pool), and each party settles independently without affecting the others.

## Supporting Rules

- **Settlement currency** — Commissions are settled in USD. Exchange costs are borne by the Sales Partner.
- **Settlement cycle** — Commissions are calculated monthly and posted to the Partner Portal after mutual confirmation.
- **Holding period** — A holding period applies before commissions can be withdrawn. Client churn during the holding period results in automatic deduction; after the holding period, already-withdrawn amounts are not clawed back. Specific duration is set by contract.
- **Minimum sales commitment** — A minimum periodic commitment applies. Failure to meet it over consecutive periods allows Zeabur to adjust rates or terminate the contract. Specific amount is set by contract.
- **Lead attribution** — Lead attribution requires Zeabur confirmation before being locked.
- **Stage locking** — Stage ownership is locked when the deal is registered; changes require written consent from both parties.
- **Commission continuity** — Commissions continue as long as the client keeps paying; they stop when the client churns.

<Callout type="warning">
The Sales Partner path and the Referral Program cannot both apply to the same transaction — pick one per deal to avoid double-benefit conflicts.
</Callout>

## Partnership Process

<Steps>

### Contact Zeabur

Apply at [partner.zeabur.com](https://partner.zeabur.com), or reach out through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support), describing your client background and estimated engagement scale.

### Negotiate contract

The Zeabur team evaluates and negotiates specific rates, stage weights, and supporting terms with you. Individual contracts are confidential.

### Sign contract

Once terms are confirmed, sign the contract and begin deal tracking.

### Client onboarding

Help the client evaluate, test, and go live.

### Monthly settlement

Once the client's payment succeeds, monthly commissions are settled per the contract.

</Steps>

## Related Addenda

Some partnerships involve separate contracts or addenda, such as:

- **Payment collection service fees** — If you act as a payment collector, the associated service fees are governed by a separate contract.
- **Education subsidies** — Partnerships involving schools or educational institutions are handled via a separate addendum/MOU.

## How to Apply

- Sign up at [partner.zeabur.com](https://partner.zeabur.com) and submit an application with your company information, client background, and estimated engagement scale.
- You can also reach out through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support) to express interest.

# Redeem Prepaid Card

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/partner/sales-partner/redeem-card.mdx

title: Redeem Prepaid Card
ogImageTitle: Redeem Prepaid Card

import { Callout, Steps } from 'nextra/components'

# Redeem Prepaid Card

Zeabur prepaid cards (Vouchers) are sold or gifted by third-party partners and can be redeemed to your Zeabur account balance. Your balance can then be used to upgrade to a paid plan, purchase dedicated servers, or pay for shared cluster usage.

<Callout type="info">
If you received an **Event Code** — for example from attending a workshop, hackathon, or instructor-led course — see the [Redeem Event Code](/partner/event-partner/redeem-event-code) instead. Event Codes and prepaid cards are different mechanisms.
</Callout>

## How to Redeem

<Steps>

### Log in to Zeabur

Log in or create an account at [zeabur.com/login](https://zeabur.com/login).

### Go to Billing

Click your avatar in the top-right and choose "Billing", or go directly to [zeabur.com/account/billing](https://zeabur.com/account/billing).

### Click "Redeem Credits"

Find the "Redeem Credits" button in the upper-right corner of the "Account Balance" section and click it.

### Enter the Card Code

Enter your prepaid card code in the dialog, then click "Redeem". On success, you'll see a notification in the bottom-right corner and your account balance will update immediately.

</Steps>

## If You Encounter Problems

- **Expired prepaid card** — Confirm the validity period with the issuer. Expired cards cannot be recovered.
- **Invalid code** — Double-check for typos and correct capitalization.
- **Other issues** — Contact customer support through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

# Dev Plan (Developer Plan)

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/pricing/dev-plan.mdx

title: Dev Plan (Developer Plan)
ogImageTitle: Dev Plan
ogImageSubtitle: Zeabur Developer Plan details

# Dev Plan (Developer Plan)

The Dev Plan is Zeabur's entry-level paid tier, designed for individual developers. At **US$5/month** with a **14-day free trial**, it unlocks Zeabur AI, automated database backups, domain purchase, and the Zeabur Email service — ideal for personal production projects and side projects.

For the full feature list and the latest quotas, see the [comparison chart](/pricing).

## Use Cases

- **Personal side projects** — Deploy personal websites, blogs, API services, etc.
- **Development & testing** — Environments that need persistent storage (e.g., databases) and automated backups.
- **Small production services** — Low-traffic services that need to run 24/7.
- **Template development** — Create and maintain Zeabur templates with [Deploy Buttons](/deploy/methods/deploy-button) to promote your projects.

## When to Upgrade to Pro

If you need **log forwarding**, **larger Email/Domain/API Key/Webhook quotas**, **custom service icons**, or **priority support**, the [Pro Plan](/pricing/pro-plan) (US$19/month, 14-day free trial) is the next step. See the [Pro Plan](/pricing/pro-plan) page for details.

## How to Subscribe

Go to [zeabur.com/pricing](https://zeabur.com/pricing) and select Dev Plan, or upgrade from the [Dashboard billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing). Credit card and Alipay are supported — see [Payment Methods](/subscription/payment-methods) for details.

# Free Plan

# Free Plan

The Free Plan is Zeabur's free tier, designed for personal exploration and learning. No credit card required — just sign up and start deploying.

For the full feature list and the latest limits, see the [comparison chart](/pricing).

## Limitations

- **Auto-sleep** — Services on the Free Plan automatically sleep after a period of inactivity. They wake up on the next incoming request, which may cause a few seconds of cold-start latency.
- **No SLA** — The Free Plan does not include a Service Level Agreement.
- **No Zeabur Email** — Sending email through [Zeabur Email](/email) is not available on the Free Plan.
- **No automated database backup/import or log forwarding** — these advanced operational features start at the Dev Plan.

<Callout type="info">
Services on the Free Plan auto-sleep when idle to conserve resources. If you need services to run continuously, consider upgrading to the [Dev Plan](/pricing/dev-plan).
</Callout>

## Upgrade Path

When your needs exceed the Free Plan, you can upgrade to a paid plan:

- **[Dev Plan](/pricing/dev-plan)** — US$5/month (14-day free trial), ideal for individual developers with personal production projects.
- **[Pro Plan](/pricing/pro-plan)** — US$19/month (14-day free trial), recommended for production workloads.
- **[Team Plan](/pricing/team-plan)** — US$79/month for 3 seats (+US$24/seat), designed for team collaboration.
- **Enterprise** — Custom plans with dedicated support and SLAs — [contact us](https://zeabur.com/support) for details.

Visit [zeabur.com/pricing](https://zeabur.com/pricing) to compare all plans.

# Pricing

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/pricing/pricing-plans.mdx

title: Pricing
ogImageTitle: Pricing
ogImageSubtitle: Zeabur Pricing

# Pricing

Zeabur offers four subscription tiers plus a custom Enterprise option:

- **[Free Plan](/pricing/free-plan)** — US$0/month. For personal exploration and learning.
- **[Dev Plan](/pricing/dev-plan)** — US$5/month, 14-day free trial. For individual developers and side projects.
- **[Pro Plan](/pricing/pro-plan)** — US$19/month, 14-day free trial. Recommended for production workloads.
- **[Team Plan](/pricing/team-plan)** — US$79/month for 3 seats, +US$24/seat. For team collaboration.
- **Enterprise** — Custom pricing — [contact us](https://zeabur.com/support) for details.

For the full feature comparison and the latest pricing, visit [zeabur.com/pricing](https://zeabur.com/pricing).

## Refunds

For any refund issues, please contact us through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

For the **Dev Plan** or **Pro Plan**, you can cancel your subscription at any time. After cancelling, you keep all features of your current plan until the end of the current billing cycle, after which your account switches to the Free plan automatically. Fees already charged for the current cycle are not refunded.

For the **Team Plan**, you can cancel your subscription at any time. After cancelling, your team retains all Team features until the end of the current billing cycle, after which the workspace is downgraded automatically. Fees already charged for the current cycle are not refunded.

For **Server** users, Zeabur no longer supports refunds for servers created or renewed after July 21, 2025. To avoid being charged in the upcoming billing cycle, you can disable the auto-renewal settings.

> Please be noted, this only affects the servers created or renewed after July 21, 2025.

![disable auto renewal](/billing/pricing/auto-renewal.png)

You can choose to receive your refund as Zeabur credits or back to your original payment method. If you opt for Zeabur credits, the refund is usually processed instantly after approval. If you choose to refund to your original payment method, it may take up to 7 days to process, and you will need to pay the Stripe transaction fee, which is approximately 30% of the amount refunded.

# Pro Plan

# Pro Plan

The Pro Plan is Zeabur's recommended tier for production workloads — **US$19/month** with a **14-day free trial**. It builds on the Dev Plan with **log forwarding**, **larger CI specs**, **longer log retention**, **higher Email/Domain/API Key/Webhook quotas**, **custom service icons**, and **priority support**.

For the full feature list and the latest quotas, see the [comparison chart](/pricing).

## Use Cases

- **Small production deployments** — Services that benefit from longer log retention, larger CI builds, and direct support channels.
- **Apps with higher transactional email volume** — The Pro Plan's monthly Email quota covers most early-stage SaaS and e-commerce apps.
- **Operations-heavy workloads** — Log forwarding to your existing observability stack (Datadog, Grafana, etc.) keeps Pro-tier services aligned with your central monitoring.
- **Frontend-heavy apps with many domains** — Pro's domain and API key headroom covers most multi-environment setups.

## When to Upgrade to Team

If you need **multiple members collaborating on the same projects**, **role and permission management**, **invoicing / tax ID support**, or **unlimited external server bindings**, the [Team Plan](/pricing/team-plan) (US$79/month for 3 seats, +US$24/seat) is the next step.

<Callout type="info">
For larger-scale custom plans, dedicated support, and SLAs, check out the **Enterprise Plan** — [contact us](https://zeabur.com/support) for details.
</Callout>

## How to Subscribe

Go to [zeabur.com/pricing](https://zeabur.com/pricing) and select Pro Plan, or upgrade from the [Dashboard billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing). Credit card and Alipay are supported — see [Payment Methods](/subscription/payment-methods) for details.

# Team Plan

The Team Plan is Zeabur's collaborative plan built for small teams that need **collaboration, unlimited server binding, and priority support**. It starts at **US$79/month** with 3 seats included, and each additional seat costs **US$24/month**.

<Callout type="warning">
The Team plan does **not** include a free trial. Start a trial on Dev or Pro if you'd like to evaluate the platform first.
</Callout>

## Plan Details

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Monthly fee | US$79 / month (3 seats included) |
| Extra seat | +US$24 / seat / month |
| Bound external servers | Unlimited |
| Build CI spec | 4C8G |
| Log retention | 90 days |
| File upload limit | High |
| Container file management | Single file + batch operations |
| HA service deployment | Supported |
| Advanced log search & drain | Supported |
| Domain & IP access control | Supported |
| Plan seats | 3 seats included (each at Pro level) |
| Role & permission management | Supported |
| Team project collaboration | Supported |
| Priority support | Supported |
| Enterprise procurement & invoicing | Supported |

## Seat Model

Team Plan supports multi-member collaboration, and every seat has Pro-level features. The base subscription includes **3 seats**; additional seats are **US$24 per seat per month**. For example, a 5-person team created on April 1 is billed `$79 + 2 × $24 = $127 / month` on the 1st of every month.

Adding or removing members does not generate a separate invoice immediately — charges are consolidated into the next billing cycle's invoice. The first 3 seats are free; billing only kicks in starting with the 4th member. When a new member joins, no charge is issued at that moment; the next invoice will bill both the "prorated amount from the join date through the end of the current cycle" and the "full seat fee for the next cycle".

Using the same 5-person Team as an example, if a 6th member is added on April 15, the May 1 invoice will add `$24 × (16 ÷ 30) + $24 ≈ $36.8` for that member.

When a member is removed, the released seat remains reserved until the end of the current billing cycle. During that window a new member can take the vacated seat at no additional cost. Fees already charged in the current cycle are non-refundable, but the seat's entitlements remain fully valid until the cycle ends. The next invoice is recalculated based on the actual number of members exceeding 3 seats.

Using the same 5-person Team as an example, if a member is removed on April 20, the 5th seat is reserved until April 30: if a new member joins on April 25, the May 1 invoice still charges `$127` for 5 seats; if no one fills the seat, starting May 1 the team is billed for 4 seats at `$79 + 1 × $24 = $103 / month`.

## Seat Roles & Permissions

Team Plan seats come in three roles: **Viewer**, **Editor**, and **Admin**. Assign roles based on what each member needs to do — read-only visibility, day-to-day development work, or full administrative control.

| Capability | Viewer | Editor (Coming soon) | Admin |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| View team members | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Invite new members | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Change member roles | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove members | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Delete the team | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View projects / services | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create projects / services | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Modify service configuration | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete projects / services | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View deployment history | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Trigger deployments manually | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Rollback deployments | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| View logs | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Search logs | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Download logs | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| View databases / servers | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create databases / servers | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Modify databases / servers | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete databases / servers | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View billing | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Change payment method | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Change subscription plan | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

- **Viewer** — read-only access across the team's resources. Best for stakeholders, auditors, or new hires during onboarding.
- **Editor** _(Coming soon)_ — can build and ship: create/modify projects, trigger deploys, rollback, search and download logs. Cannot delete resources or manage members/billing.
- **Admin** — full administrative control, including member management, destructive operations, and billing. Required for any action that affects the team itself or its subscription.

## What's included (vs. Pro)

Everything in Pro, plus:

- **Unlimited** bound external servers (Pro: 10)
- **90 days** of log retention (Pro: 30 days)
- **3 seats included** (each at Pro level)
- **Team project collaboration**
- **Role & permission management**
- **Priority customer & technical support**
- **Batch file operations** on containers
- **Enterprise procurement & invoicing**

## Invoicing & Tax ID

The Team Plan supports formal invoice issuance and tax ID configuration, suitable for businesses and organizations that need receipts for accounting. See [Invoicing](/subscription/invoicing) for details.

## Pro Plan vs. Team Plan

| Feature | Pro Plan | Team Plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly fee | US$19 | US$79 (3 seats) + US$24 / extra seat |
| Bound external servers | 10 | Unlimited |
| Log retention | 30 days | 90 days |
| Plan seats | 1 | 3 (each at Pro level) |
| Role & permission management | — | Supported |
| Team collaboration | — | Supported |
| Priority support | — | Supported |
| Enterprise procurement & invoicing | — | Supported |
| Free trial | 14 days | Not available |
| Best for | Individual developers | Teams / organizations |

<Callout type="info">
For larger-scale custom plans, dedicated technical resources, and enterprise contracts, see the **Enterprise Plan** — [contact us](https://zeabur.com/support) for details.
</Callout>

## Use Cases

- **Startup teams** — Multiple developers jointly managing deployment environments.
- **Enterprise internal projects** — Teams that need unified billing and formal invoicing.
- **Agencies** — Separate projects for different clients, unified under one team.
- **Open-source communities** — Multiple maintainers collaborating on service deployments.

## How to Subscribe

Go to [zeabur.com/pricing](https://zeabur.com/pricing) and select Team Plan, or upgrade from the [Dashboard billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing). Credit card and Alipay are supported — see [Payment Methods](/subscription/payment-methods) for details.

**PERSONAL DATA** means data about a living individual who can be identified from those data (or from those and other information either in our possession or likely to come into our possession).

# Contribution Reward Program

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/rewards/contribution.mdx

title: Contribution Reward Program
ogImageTitle: Contribution Reward Program
ogImageSubtitle: Create templates that people actually use and earn free usage credits!

# Contribution Reward Program

To encourage developers to help Zeabur build a high-quality [template](https://zeabur.com/templates) ecosystem, we offer the "Contribution Reward Program" to provide free usage credits to template authors whose templates are actively used by the community.

*This program takes effect on June 1, 2026. Only templates created on or after this date are eligible.*

## How It Works

Rewards are based entirely on **unique user deployments** — the number of distinct users who have deployed your template. Creating a template alone does not earn any reward; only real usage counts.

### Reward Tiers

| Milestone | Reward | Cumulative |
|-----------|--------|------------|
| 50+ unique users | $10 | $10 |
| 100+ unique users | $20 | $30 |
| 500+ unique users | $60 | $90 |
| 2,000+ unique users | $150 | $240 |
| 10,000+ unique users | $300 | $540 |

Rewards are cumulative. For example, a template reaching 500+ unique users earns a total of **$90** ($10 + $20 + $60). Each milestone is paid out once per template. Deleting and recreating a template (including same upstream project, same functionality, or renamed variants) does not reset milestone progress.

### Template Requirements

To be eligible for rewards, your template must meet **all** of the following:

1. The template must not duplicate existing templates unless it is a new version or intended for a different scenario or purpose.
2. The template must include complete information, including the template name, description, cover image, introduction, and usage instructions.
3. The template introduction must have at least an English version.
4. The template must be deployable with one click. If extra steps are needed after deployment, those must be documented in the template introduction.

Refer to [Creating Templates from YAML](../template/template-format) to learn how to create templates.

## How to Claim Rewards

Once your template reaches a milestone, please let us know through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support) and we will grant the corresponding credits.

# Referral Program

Zeabur offers a referral program to all users. By sharing your referral code, you can provide discounts to referred users while earning commission rewards.

## Tier System

The referral program uses a five-tier system that automatically upgrades based on your cumulative referred revenue:

| Tier | Threshold | Referee Discount | Referrer Commission |
|------|-----------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Lv1 | $0 | 10% | 20% |
| Lv2 | $100 | 20% | 40% |
| Lv3 | $500 | 30% | 60% |
| Lv4 | $1,000 | 40% | 80% |
| Lv5 | $5,000 | 50% | 100% |

- **Referee Discount**: The discount percentage the referred user receives on applicable products.
- **Referrer Commission**: The commission percentage earned by the referrer (based on the referee's actual payment amount).

## Applicable Products

Referral codes currently apply to the following product types:

- **RENT_SERVER** (Server Rental) — Triggered on first purchase only.
- ~~**AIHUB_TOPUP** (AI Hub Top-up) — One-time trigger only.~~

<Callout type="warning">
Upstream model providers have updated their billing model. Starting June 2026, **AI Hub top-ups are no longer eligible for the referral program**.
</Callout>

<Callout>
Each referred user can only use a referral code once per product type.
</Callout>

## Referral Code Rules

The following conditions must be met when using a referral code:

- **No self-referral**: You cannot use your own referral code.
- **Referrer eligibility**: The referrer's account must have at least one Project containing a Service.
- **Uniqueness**: The referee must not have previously used any referral code for that product type.

## How to Invite Friends

You can find your referral code and referral link on the [Referral page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/referral). Copy and share it with friends via email, social media, or any other channel.

## Referral Wallet

Commissions earned through referrals accumulate in your Referral Wallet. Accumulated commissions can be converted to Stripe Credits, which can be used to pay for your Zeabur subscriptions and usage fees.

## Check Referral Status

You can view your current referral status and commission history on the [Referral page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/referral).

![Referral](/referral/referral.png)

The page displays two types of referral status:

- **Pending**: The referred user has signed up using your referral code but has not yet completed a payment.
- **Credited**: The referred user has completed a payment, and the commission has been added to your wallet.

## KOL Override

For KOLs (Key Opinion Leaders) with significant reach, Zeabur administrators can set custom discount and commission percentages that override the tier system. If you are interested, please contact us via [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

## How to Use Your Credits

Your credits are used with the highest priority when paying. Usage fees and subscription costs will be deducted from your credits first. Only after credits are exhausted will charges be applied to your linked payment method.

<Callout type="info">
**Legacy Referral System**: Under the previous referral program, each successful referral that upgraded to a paid plan earned $5 USD in Credits. This legacy system is expected to be consolidated with the new tier system by Q2 2026. Both systems operate in parallel until the consolidation is complete.
</Callout>

# Security Practices

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/security-practices.mdx

title: Security Practices
ogImageTitle: Security Practices
ogImageSubtitle: How Zeabur protects your data and infrastructure

# Security Practices

## Compliance

Zeabur is currently pursuing **SOC 2 Type II** certification. Our compliance program covers the Trust Services Criteria for security, availability, and confidentiality. We are committed to achieving and maintaining industry-recognized certifications as we scale.

## Infrastructure Security

Zeabur operates across multiple globally distributed infrastructure providers to deliver reliable, low-latency services:

- Amazon Web Services (AWS)
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
- Hetzner
- Linode (Akamai)
- DigitalOcean
- Tencent Cloud
- Alibaba Cloud
- Volcengine
- Glows.ai

All infrastructure providers are selected for their established security postures, physical data center protections, and compliance certifications. Zeabur leverages provider-native security features including network isolation, firewall rules, and DDoS mitigation across all regions.

## Data Encryption

### In Transit

All data transmitted between customers and Zeabur is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher. This applies to all API endpoints, dashboard access, and service-to-service communication within the platform. Customer-facing services deployed on Zeabur are served over HTTPS with automatic certificate provisioning.

### At Rest

Production data is stored in MongoDB Atlas, which provides encryption at rest by default using AES-256 encryption. Access to production databases is restricted to devices connected via Tailscale.

## Access Control

### Identity and Authentication

- All employees authenticate through Google Workspace with two-factor authentication (2FA) enforced.
- Access to production databases and internal systems requires connection via Tailscale, and only approved users may add devices to the network.

### Endpoint Security

- Zeabur is implementing mobile device management (MDM) to bring all company devices under centralized management.
- Only Tailscale-approved devices can access internal pages and production databases.

### Least Privilege

- Team members are granted the minimum level of access required to perform their responsibilities.
- Access to production infrastructure, databases, and customer environments is restricted and audited.
- Access permissions are reviewed periodically and revoked promptly upon role changes or offboarding.

## Secure Development

Zeabur integrates security throughout the software development lifecycle:

- **Code Review**: All code changes require peer review via pull requests before merging to production branches.
- **CI/CD Pipelines**: Automated build, test, and deployment pipelines enforce quality and security checks on every change.
- **Dependency Scanning**: Automated scanning for known vulnerabilities in third-party dependencies, with alerts for critical issues.
- **Environment Separation**: Development, staging, and production environments are logically separated to prevent unauthorized access to production data.

## Incident Response

Zeabur maintains a documented incident response plan that covers:

- **Detection and Alerting**: Monitoring and alerting systems are in place to detect anomalies, unauthorized access, and infrastructure failures.
- **Triage and Response**: A defined process for classifying incidents by severity, assigning ownership, and coordinating response efforts.
- **Communication**: Affected customers are notified promptly in the event of a security incident that impacts their data or services.
- **Post-Incident Review**: All significant incidents are followed by a post-mortem analysis to identify root causes and implement preventive measures.

## Data Handling and Privacy

- Customer data is processed solely to provide and operate the Services as requested by the customer.
- Zeabur does not sell, rent, or lease customer data to third parties.
- Upon account termination, customer data is retained for 7 days to allow for export, after which it is permanently deleted.
- For full details, see our [Privacy Policy](/docs/en-US/privacy-policy).

## Network Security

- All customer workloads run in isolated containers with network-level separation.
- Ingress and egress traffic is filtered and monitored.
- Internal service communication is restricted to authorized endpoints.
- Cloudflare is used for edge security, CDN, and DDoS protection on customer-facing domains.

## Physical Security

Zeabur relies on the physical security controls of our infrastructure providers. All data center facilities used by Zeabur maintain industry-standard physical security measures including biometric access controls, 24/7 surveillance, and environmental protections. Refer to each provider's compliance documentation for details.

## Responsible Disclosure

If you discover a security vulnerability in Zeabur, please report it to [contact@zeabur.com](mailto:contact@zeabur.com). We take all reports seriously and will investigate and respond promptly. We ask that you give us reasonable time to address the issue before public disclosure.

---

# Server

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Server

Beyond shared clusters, you can **register your own server with Zeabur** and let Zeabur handle service deployment, firewall rules, and resource allocation on your hardware — no manual SSH required.

## Why Use a Server

- **Exclusive resources**: Your services don't share hardware with other users, so performance is stable and predictable.
- **Bring Your Own Hardware (BYOH)**: Already running servers on AWS, GCP, Hetzner, or your own datacenter? Mount them to Zeabur in one click and get full deployment management capabilities.
- **Geographic flexibility**: Cover regions not yet served by shared clusters using your own infrastructure.
- **High-reliability production**: For large systems with strict SLA and security requirements.

## What Zeabur Manages for You

Once registered, you can handle all of the following from the Zeabur Dashboard — without touching the host directly:

- Deploy and update services
- View real-time logs and performance metrics
- Set environment variables
- Manage persistent storage and network settings

<Callout type="info">
  Servers are billed monthly at a fixed rate, not by resource usage. Best suited for production workloads with stable hardware requirements.
</Callout>

## Get Started

1. **[Purchase a Server](/en-US/server/purchase)** — Buy a server from Zeabur with competitive pricing
2. **[Add a Server](/en-US/server/register)** — Mount an existing server to Zeabur
3. **[Manage Your Server](/en-US/server/operate)** — Configure firewall, monitor resources, adjust settings

## FAQ

### Do I need a subscription plan to use a server?

No, you do not need a subscription plan to use a server. However, we recommend the Developer Plan to unleash the full potential of Zeabur — features like backup are only available to Developer Plan subscribers. Developer Plan users also receive priority support from staff, while free users can get help through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support) without a guaranteed response time. See [Plans](/en-US/pricing/pricing-plans) for details.

### I only want to host small websites — do I need both a plan and a server?

You can deploy services on a server without a subscription plan. However, certain features such as backup are exclusive to the Developer Plan. If you want full access to Zeabur's platform capabilities and priority support, we recommend subscribing to the Developer Plan alongside your server. For more information, see [Community & Support](/en-US/get-started/faq-support).

# Firewall & Security Settings

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/server/firewall.mdx

title: Firewall & Security Settings
ogImageTitle: Firewall & Security Settings
ogImageSubtitle: Configure firewall rules and security settings for your server

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Firewall & Security Settings

<Callout type="info">
The firewall management features described on this page may still be under development or only available for certain servers. Refer to the Dashboard interface for the actual available settings.
</Callout>

Zeabur provides server-level firewall management, allowing you to configure inbound rules directly from the Dashboard without SSH-ing into the server to manage iptables manually.

## Overview

Each [server](/server) has its own firewall configuration. By default, Zeabur opens the ports required for services to operate (such as 80 and 443) and blocks all other unauthorized inbound connections.

<Callout type="info">
Firewall rules only control **inbound traffic**. Outbound connections from your services are not restricted by the firewall.
</Callout>

## Configuring Firewall Rules

1. Go to the [Zeabur Servers page](https://zeabur.com/servers) and select your server.
2. Click the "**Firewall**" tab in the left navigation.
3. Click the "**Add Rule**" button to create an inbound rule.

Each rule requires the following fields:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Protocol | TCP or UDP |
| Port Range | A single port (e.g., `8080`) or a range (e.g., `3000-3100`) |
| Source IP | Allowed source IP address or CIDR block (e.g., `203.0.113.0/24`); leave empty to allow all sources |

Click "**Save**" when done. Rules take effect within seconds.

## IP Allowlisting and Blocklisting

- **Allowlist mode**: To restrict access to specific IPs for a given port, simply specify the source IP when creating a rule.
- **Blocklist mode**: Zeabur's firewall uses an allowlist strategy (default-deny). Ports and sources not explicitly opened in a rule are blocked, so no separate blocklist configuration is needed.

### Common Scenarios

**Allow only office IP to access admin panel**

| Protocol | Port | Source IP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TCP | 8443 | `203.0.113.10` |

**Open database port for a specific subnet**

| Protocol | Port | Source IP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TCP | 5432 | `10.0.0.0/16` |

## Required Ports

The following ports are required for Zeabur to operate properly. Do not block them:

| Port | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| 22 | SSH management |
| 80 | HTTP traffic |
| 443 | HTTPS traffic |
| 4222 | NATS internal communication |
| 6443 | K3s API Server |
| 30000–32767 | Kubernetes NodePort range |

<Callout type="warning">
Blocking any of these ports may prevent Zeabur from managing your server or cause services to become unreachable.
</Callout>

## Security Best Practices

- **Principle of least privilege** — Only open the ports and source IPs you actually need. Avoid using `0.0.0.0/0` (allow all) for sensitive services.
- **Audit rules regularly** — Periodically review your firewall rules and remove ports that are no longer needed.
- **Use private networking** — For inter-service communication, use [private networking](/deploy/networking/private-networking) to avoid transmitting sensitive data over the public internet.
- **Keep SSH secure** — Use SSH key authentication instead of passwords, and consider restricting SSH access to specific IPs.

# Maintain your Server

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/server/operate.mdx

title: Maintain Server
ogImageTitle: Maintain Server
ogImageSubtitle: Maintain your Server

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components';

# Maintain your Server

This article will introduce how to maintain your [server](../server) registered with Zeabur.

<Callout>
    If you purchased a server from Zeabur, the operation and maintenance tasks are performed by us.
    Please submit a ticket to let us know which project you want to maintain, and our staff will handle it for you.
</Callout>

## Space Cleanup

If you find that the disk space on your host is insufficient, you can try cleaning up the Docker images pulled by K3s on your host (this is usually done automatically).

```bash
# Check which images have been pulled (no need to type this line)
$ sudo k3s crictl images

# Remove all unused images
$ sudo k3s crictl rmi --prune
```

Sometimes, the logs recorded by K3s for each container can also take up a lot of space. You can try cleaning these logs in the [K3s logs directory](https://docs.k3s.io/faq#where-are-the-k3s-logs).

## Mounting a Volume on a Dedicated Server

If you want to expand persistent storage for a Dedicated Server, you can mount an additional disk to `/var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage` on the server itself. This is a host-level maintenance operation. You can use the **SSH** entry in the left sidebar of the Zeabur server page to enter the server and run the required commands.

For example, you can use the following command to mount an additional disk to `/var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage`:

```bash
sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage
```

Replace `/dev/sdb1` with your actual disk partition name.

If you want the disk to remain mounted after a server reboot, you can add the mount entry to `/etc/fstab`. Using a UUID is recommended over a device path like `/dev/sdb1`, as device names can change across reboots or hardware changes. Use `blkid` to find the UUID:

```bash
sudo blkid /dev/sdb1
```

Then add the entry using the UUID:

```bash
echo 'UUID=<your-partition-uuid> /var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage ext4 defaults,nofail 0 2' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
```

Replace `<your-partition-uuid>` and `ext4` with your actual partition UUID and filesystem type. After updating `/etc/fstab`, we recommend running the following command to verify the configuration:

```bash
sudo mount -a
```

After the mount is complete, the disk space will be used as shared storage for services on the entire Dedicated Server.

<Callout type="warning">
    This operation will make the existing contents of `/var/lib/rancher/k3s/storage` inaccessible while the volume is mounted (they are hidden, not deleted, and will reappear if the volume is unmounted). It will also affect any persistent data currently relying on that path. Make sure to back up the relevant data first, and perform this during a maintenance window or migration to avoid service interruption or data loss.
</Callout>

## Recovering from OOM (Server Offline)

If your server runs out of memory (OOM), the K3s status indicator on the server dashboard may turn red, meaning Kubernetes is no longer running properly. When this happens, your services will become unreachable.

![Server Info showing K3s status](/server/server-info.png)

To recover, go to **Settings** and click **Reboot Server**.

![Reboot Server button in Settings](/server/reboot-server-button.png)

A dialog will appear listing all services that will automatically restart after the reboot. **If K3s is red (offline), we recommend deselecting all services** to prevent the server from immediately running out of memory again after restarting.

![Reboot Server dialog with services listed](/server/reboot-dialog.png)

Click **Deselect All** to prevent any services from auto-starting, then click **Reboot**.

![Reboot Server dialog with all services deselected](/server/reboot-deselected.png)

<Callout type="warning">
    The reboot process takes about 3–5 minutes. Once the server restarts, K3s should return to green. After confirming the server is healthy, you can re-enable services one by one from the **Projects** tab.
</Callout>

If your server frequently goes OOM, consider upgrading to a larger server or reducing the number of services deployed. You should also configure **Resource Reservation** (see below) to prevent the system from being completely starved of resources.

## Resource Reservation

Resource Reservation allows you to reserve CPU and memory for Kubernetes and system processes, ensuring the server stays reachable even under heavy load. This prevents OOM situations where the operating system or Kubernetes itself gets killed.

Go to **Settings** > **Advanced Settings** > **Resource Reservation**.

![Resource Reservation settings](/server/resource-reservation.png)

There are two categories of reservation:

- **Kubernetes Reserved**: Resources reserved for Kubernetes system components (kubelet, kube-proxy, etc.)
- **System Reserved**: Resources reserved for OS-level processes (SSH, systemd, etc.)

<Callout type="info">
    Newly purchased servers default to 500m CPU / 512Mi memory for both Kubernetes and system reservations. We recommend keeping these defaults to ensure server stability. If you previously purchased a server without these defaults, consider setting them manually.
</Callout>

After adjusting the values, click **Save** to apply the changes.

## Changing DNS Nameservers

By default, Zeabur's servers use [Cloudflare DNS](https://1.1.1.1/) as the DNS nameservers for the cluster (machines in mainland China use [Alibaba Cloud Public DNS](https://www.alidns.com/)).

If you need to change the DNS nameservers used by the cluster (for example, to Tencent Cloud's [DNSPod Public DNS](https://www.dnspod.cn/products/publicdns)), you can edit `/etc/resolv.kubelet.conf` and change the `nameserver` to the DNS nameservers you want.

```
nameserver 119.29.29.29
```

Remember to restart the K3s service after making changes.

```bash
$ sudo systemctl restart k3s
```

## Disabling Zeabur Services

If you own a server, you can disable all Zeabur services and use the VPS freely for other purposes, such as running Docker Compose services.

<Callout type="warning">
    Disabling Zeabur services means you will not be able to create projects and services from the Zeabur dashboard, and any services currently running on Zeabur will stop. However, you can still manage server settings such as firewall rules and reboots. Note that reinstalling the server from Zeabur will reinstall and re-enable Zeabur services.
</Callout>

### Disable Zeabur Services

You can also click the **SSH** option in the Zeabur Dashboard sidebar to connect to your server directly from the browser, no local terminal required:

![SSH into server from Zeabur Dashboard](/server/server-ssh-from-dashboard.webp)

Or connect via SSH and run:

```bash
sudo systemctl disable --now k3s containerd
```

> Note: Stopping these services will cause all containers and services running on the server to stop. Please proceed with caution.

### Re-enable Zeabur Services

If you want to bring Zeabur back online, connect via SSH and run:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now k3s containerd
```

## Using VS Code for Remote Development

You can use [VS Code Remote - SSH](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh) to connect to your server and directly edit files or operate containers in a familiar IDE environment.

### Step 1: Install the Remote-SSH Extension

Open VS Code and install the **Remote - SSH** extension from the Extensions Marketplace.

### Step 2: Set Up SSH Key Authentication

Generate an SSH key pair on your local machine (if you don't have one) and add the public key to the server:

```bash
# Generate an SSH key pair on your local machine
$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519

# Copy the public key to the server
$ ssh-copy-id <username>@<server-ip>
```

If `ssh-copy-id` is not available, you can manually append the public key:

```bash
$ cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | ssh <username>@<server-ip> "mkdir -p ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys"
```

### Step 3: Connect via VS Code

Open the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`), select **Remote-SSH: Connect to Host**, and enter `<username>@<server-ip>` to connect.

### Step 4: Locate the Service's File Storage Path

After connecting, you will be at the server's root directory. To find where your service's files are stored, first locate the PVC (Persistent Volume Claim) for your service, then find the corresponding PV (Persistent Volume) and its host path.

The PVC name follows the format `<volume-id>-service-<service-id>`, located in the namespace `environment-<environment-id>`.

```bash
# List all PVCs to find your service's volume
$ kubectl get pvc -A

# Find the PV that the PVC is bound to
$ kubectl get pvc <pvc-name> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}'

# Get the host path of the corresponding PV
$ kubectl get pv <pv-name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.local.path}'
```

You can then open this path in VS Code using **File → Open Folder** to start editing your service's files.

### Step 5: Access a Container Shell

To get a terminal environment inside your service's container (equivalent to the Web Terminal on Zeabur):

```bash
# List pods in a namespace
$ kubectl get pods -n <namespace>

# Open a shell in a pod
$ kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n <namespace> -- /bin/sh
```

## Uninstallation

First, you need to remove the server and the services deployed on it from Zeabur.

![Remove Server](/server/remove-server.webp)

The "Remove Server" step **will not remove the infrastructure set up by Zeabur on your server**. Zeabur's infrastructure is primarily built on [K3s](https://k3s.io/), so the uninstallation steps [follow the K3s uninstallation steps](https://docs.k3s.io/installation/uninstall).

```bash
$ /usr/local/bin/k3s-uninstall.sh
```

# Register Server

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/server/register.mdx

title: Register Server
ogImageTitle: Register Server
ogImageSubtitle: Register a server on Zeabur

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components';

# Register Server

This article will explain how to register a [Server](../server) on Zeabur. If you don't have your own server, you can [purchase one from Zeabur](./purchase) instead.

## Prerequisites

- You already have a server, and this server must have at least one public IP address that can be connected to.
- The server must have at least 1 CPU core and at least 2 GB of memory.
- The server must have the following ports open: `22`, `80`, `443`, `4222`, `6443`, `30000-32767`.
- The server must allow SSH login, and the username must be `root`.
- This server must allow login using the `root` user or another user who can use `sudo`, either through a password or SSH key.

<Callout type="default">
    If you are not using the `root` user, considering that Zeabur configures the machine in a non-interactive environment (unable to enter the password on your behalf), please ensure that the `sudo` user group to which your user belongs has been granted the tag, [`NOPASSWD`](https://linux.die.net/man/5/sudoers).
</Callout>

## Registration Steps

![add machine to zeabur](/server/add-machine-to-zeabur.webp)

1. After logging into Zeabur, click on "My Servers" in the top navigation bar or at the top of the project list page, or directly visit [https://zeabur.com/servers](https://zeabur.com/servers).
2. Click the "Create" button in the upper right corner of the page, then select "Connect your own Server".
3. Enter the server's IP address and SSH port (default is `22`).
4. Enter the username (e.g., `root`), then choose the login method (password or SSH key).
5. If you choose a password, enter the password below; if you choose an SSH key, enter the SSH key below.

<Callout type="warning">
    Zeabur only accepts SSH keys in **OpenSSH format** (the private key starts with `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`). Some cloud providers, such as Tencent Cloud, provide SSH keys in the legacy RSA PEM format (`-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`) by default, which will cause an SSH connection failure. To convert your key to OpenSSH format, run:

    ```bash
    ssh-keygen -p -N "" -f /path/to/your_private_key
    ```

    After conversion, paste the updated key content into the SSH key field.
</Callout>

6. Click the "Add Server" button and wait for the server registration to complete (this process takes about 30 seconds).
7. After successful registration, you will see the newly registered server in the server list.
8. Wait about a minute until the status shows "Online" and the CPU and memory usage can be displayed normally.

If you encounter registration failure, please report it to us through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).

## Maintain your Server

Please refer to our [Maintain Server](./operate) document, to learn how to maintain your server.

---

# Shared Cluster (Deprecated)

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/server/shared-cluster.mdx

title: Shared Cluster (Deprecated)
ogImageTitle: Shared Cluster (Deprecated)
ogImageSubtitle: Historical shared cluster information and migration guide

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components'

# Shared Cluster (Deprecated)

<Callout type="error">
Shared clusters have been deprecated. New projects can no longer be created on shared clusters, and existing shared cluster projects stopped accepting new services on **April 1, 2026**. All new projects should use [Servers](/server).
</Callout>

## What was the Shared Cluster

The shared cluster was Zeabur's early server offering. In this model, multiple users' services were deployed on the same Kubernetes cluster, sharing underlying CPU, memory, and network resources. Users didn't need to manage hardware and only paid for actual resource usage.

## Shared Cluster vs. Server

| Feature | Shared Cluster (Deprecated) | Server |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resource Isolation | Multi-tenant, shared hardware | Fully dedicated hardware |
| Billing | Usage-based (vCPU / memory / traffic) | Fixed monthly fee |
| Server Location | Fixed regions (AWS, GCP) | Bring Your Own Host (BYOH), any region |
| Performance Stability | Potential noisy-neighbor effects | Stable and predictable |
| Use Case | Small projects, dev/test | Production, high-reliability workloads |

## Why It Was Discontinued

As the server offering matured, Zeabur consolidated the shared cluster into the server architecture to provide better resource isolation and performance guarantees.

## Migrating from Shared Cluster to Server

If your services are still running on a shared cluster, follow these steps to migrate:

1. **Provision a server** — Purchase or [register your own server](/server/register) on the [Zeabur Servers page](https://zeabur.com/servers).
2. **Back up your data** — Use the [Backup & Restore](/operations/data/backup-restore) feature to create backups of all stateful services (databases, persistent storage).
3. **Export your project** — Use the [Export Project](/deploy/manage/export-project) feature to export your project's YAML configuration.
4. **Redeploy on the server** — Create a new project in the server's region, import the configuration, and redeploy your services.
5. **Restore data** — Restore the backups from step 2 into the new services.
6. **Switch DNS** — Point your custom domain's DNS records to the new service's domain.
7. **Verify and clean up** — Once the new environment is running correctly, remove the old services from the shared cluster.

<Callout type="info">
If you encounter any issues during migration, please reach out through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).
</Callout>

# Subscription

Source: https://github.com/zeabur/zeabur/blob/main/docs/pages/en-US/subscription.mdx

title: Subscription
ogImageTitle: Subscription
ogImageSubtitle: Subscription on Zeabur

import { Callout } from 'nextra/components';

# Subscription

## What is Subscription?

Zeabur offers five plans: **Free**, **Dev**, **Pro**, **Team**, and a customized **Enterprise** plan, suited to different stages of usage and needs. You can check the details of each plan on the [plans](/pricing/pricing-plans) page.

If you have not subscribed to any plan, you'll be considered a **Free Plan** user by default.

## 14-Day Free Trial

Each user is entitled to one 14-day free trial and may choose either the **Dev ($5/month)** or **Pro ($19/month)** plan. During the trial you'll have full access to all features and resource quotas of the selected plan.

No charges are incurred during the trial; once it ends, the system will automatically renew the selected plan and start billing. If you don't wish to continue, cancel the subscription before the trial ends.

Users may also end the trial early at any time to immediately begin the paid subscription — the billing cycle starts from that day. The **Team plan ($79/month)** does not include a free trial.

## How to Subscribe?

Zeabur's subscription is based on [Stripe](https://stripe.com/).

There are 2 ways to subscribe to a plan: **Credit Card** and **Prepaid Credits**.

### Subscribe with Credit Card

You can subscribe to a plan with your credit card, paying in USD.

- Setup without subscription: Go to [billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing), you can setup your credit card in **Payment Method** section. After you've input your credit card information, click **Add** button to save your credit card, then you can simply click **Subscribe** button in [plan page](https://zeabur.com/pricing#upgrade) to update your subscription.
- Setup with subscription: Go to the [plan page](https://zeabur.com/pricing#upgrade) in dashboard, choose a plan, and then input your credit card information, click **Subscribe** button, you'll be redirected to Stripe's checkout page, fill the form and you'll be subscribed to the plan with your credit card saved.

### Subscribe with Prepaid Credits

If you don't have a credit card that is compatible with Stripe service, you can subscribe to a plan with buying some credits.

Go to the [billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing) in dashboard, press the **Get More Credits** button to buy some credits, then you can go to the [plan page](https://zeabur.com/pricing#upgrade) in dashboard to upgrade your plan with the credits you've bought.

![Get More Credits](/billing/subscription/get-more-credits.png)

## How to Change Payment Method

If your card is declined or you want to change your payment method, you can do it in the [billing page](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing).

Scroll down to find the **Unbind Payment Method** to unbind current credit card, then you can setup a new credit card.

## How to Downgrade to Free Plan

If you've subscribed to a paid plan, you can downgrade to **Free Plan** at any time.

Go to [billing page in your dashboard](https://dash.zeabur.com/account/billing), scroll down to the danger zone for unsubscribing.

![Unsubscribe Plan](/billing/subscription/unsubscribe.png)

<Callout>
    By downgrading to the Free Plan, you will no longer incur any charges. However, your currently deployed Containerized services will be automatically suspended by the system.
</Callout>

## Contact us

If you have any questions about subscription, please contact us through [Zeabur Support](https://zeabur.com/support).
